FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION May 1, 2025 Graduate Council Report 2024-2025-8A At the April 25, 2025 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES ENG 410 - Capstone Seminar in Literary and Cultural Studies, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (4 crs.) A capstone course in literary and cultural studies research for English majors: requires the completion of a scholarly essay or another research-intensive project. (Lec. 3, Practicum 1).

Pre: two 300- or 400-level ENG courses (excluding 477). (B4) (D1) ENG 405 - Creative Writing Capstone, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit, Change course title and/or course description (4 crs.) A capstone course in creative writing for English majors taking the Creative Writing Option; includes workshop, portfolio creation, critical responses to texts, exploration of creative writing field. (Lec. 1, Workshop 2, Online 1) Pre: ENG 205 and 305, or two ENG 305 courses in different genres (ENG 305A, 305B, 305C, or 305D).
ENG 447 - Poetry, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (4 crs.) Study of major contributions and movements in poetry of any period. (Seminar) ENG 469 - The Novel, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (4 crs.) Focuses on generic considerations of the novel in relation to historical contexts such as national/cultural politics, philosophy, psychology.

The 'novel' is examined against the historical specificity of its production. (Seminar) ENG 472 - Shakespeare, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (4 crs.) Studies in Shakespeare's drama and poetry. (Seminar) ENG 479 - Renaissance Authors, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit

(4 crs.) Studies in works by one or more major Renaissance authors (excepting Shakespeare).
May be repeated once, barring duplication of writers. (Seminar) ENG 480 - British Restoration and Enlightenment Authors, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (4 crs.) Studies in works by one or two major Restoration and Enlightenment authors. (Seminar) May be repeated once for a total of 8 credits, barring duplication of writers.
STA 525 - Programming and Data Management in SAS, Effective Fall 2025 Add online modality to existing in-person course (4 crs.) Data managing and programming in SAS: data input, formatting and labeling, conditional processing, iterative processing, numeric and character functions, customized reports, data visualization, and basic statistical analysis. (Lec. 3, Rec. 1/Online) Pre: STA307 or STA308 or STA409 or by permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING BME 461 (ELE461) - Physiological Modeling and Control, Effective Spring 2026 Change prerequisites, corequisites (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (BME), ELE461.

Principles of physiological modeling and control of linear and nonlinear systems, stability analysis, root locus, Bode plots, linearization. (Lec. 3) Pre: ELE313, or permission of instructor.
Not open to students who have credit in ELE561.
BME 464 - Medical Imaging Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit, Effective Spring 2026 (3 crs.) Engineering and clinical applications of medical imaging systems including X-ray, computed tomography, radioisotope imaging, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging; picture archiving and communication system and medical image processing. (Lec. 3) Pre: (BME207 and BME360 and ELE313) or permission of instructor.
Not open to students who have credit in ELE564.
BME 465 - Medical Image Processing Laboratory, Effective Fall 2025 Change 400-level course to qualify for graduate credit (1 cr.) Development of medical imaging processing algorithms with graphical user interface in C++ under the Windows operating system; smoothing and sharpening filters, morphological filters, area measurement and edge tracer. (Lab. 1) Pre: credit or concurrent enrollment in BME464.
Open to students who have credit in ELE565.

BME 468 - Neural Engineering, Effective Spring 2026 Change prerequisites, corequisites (3 crs.) Principles and technologies of neuroengineering and clinical applications; brain stimulator, spinal cord stimulation, functional electrical stimulation (FES), neural-machine interface for motor prosthesis control, artificial visual/auditory devices for augmented sensory perception. (Lec. 3) Pre: BME360 or permission of instructor.
Open to graduate students who have credit in ELE568.
BME 473 - Brain Signal Processing and Applications, Effective Spring 2026 Change prerequisites, corequisites (4 crs.) Presents advanced techniques in brain signal processing including time-frequency analysis (e.g., wavelet), spatial filters (e.g., Laplacian filters), data reduction techniques (e.g., PCA), and machine learning algorithms (e.g., LDA). (Lec. 3, Rec. 1) Pre: {(MTH243 or equivalent), and (MTH451 or STA409 or ISEI31 or equivalent), and (ELE314 or equivalent), and Matlab programming} or by permission of instructor.
Familiarity with topics in ELE501, ELE506, and ELE509 is highly recommended.
Not open to students who have credit in ELE573.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES BES 593 - Internship in Science Writing Effective Fall 2025

Change in modality, add online (3 crs.) Internship with agency or organization in which student develops and disseminates written pieces on science-related topics to non-scientific audiences. (Practicum/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Previous completion of WRT533, NRS543, and permission of instructor. GEO 534 - Analytical Geochemistry, Effective Summer 2025 Change course number/level (1-3 crs.) Advanced work in analytical geochemistry under the supervision of a faculty member arranged to suit the individual requirements of the student. (Independent Study) Pre: permission of instructor. GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY OCG 551: Coastal Oceanography, Effective Fall 2026 Change in course title or description (4 crs.) Interdisciplinary study of coastal, ecosystems and oceanography. Explores marine dynamics and human coastal interactions through lectures and lab work. Instructor permission required. (Lecture 3, Lab 1) COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES PSY 434: Psychological Testing, Effective Spring 2026 Change in prerequisites, corequisites (3 crs.) Measurement procedures employed in the measurement of intelligence, aptitudes, abilities, attitudes, interests, and personality. Focus on psychometric principles associated with the various tests. (Lec. 3) Pre: PSY200 or STA307 or STA308. NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES MAF 416X (APG416X) - Aquatic Ethnoecology: Concepts and Applications, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Explores the diversity of knowledge of and beliefs about aquatic life and ecosystems among human groups, including Indigenous, Traditional, and Local Ecological Knowledge and applications to Marine/Aquatic Science and Management. (Seminar) Pre: Juniors or Seniors with credit in APG203 or MAF100; or graduate status.
